brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: 3 cells in a row with hex-acc-keyhole on rear face (slot 4) on each cell: accessory:0#-1,0#4, accessory:0#0,0#4, accessory:0#1,0#4. Keyhole slots allow screw-head mounting to wall.

6x hex-acc-hook plates (each with two hooks) on front faces slots 1 and 2 across all three cells: accessory:0#-1,0#1, accessory:0#-1,0#2, accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#0,0#2, accessory:0#1,0#1, accessory:0#1,0#2 — total 12 hook positions for pliers, screwdrivers etc.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell horizontal rack (piece: -1,0,0; 0,0,0; 1,0,0) with keyhole hangers on the wall-facing side and six hook plates (12 hooks) on the front-facing sides. End caps and joint bolts applied.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Hook plate
parts.use: Each plate carries two hooks side by side, so you bolt on as many as you want where you want them rather than committing a whole face to a rail.
